I built an AI Sales Operating System that finds leads, writes outreach, and follows up — while I sleep.

Most "AI sales automation" posts show:

Lead → GPT → Email

That's not an operating system. That's a demo.

A real system has to:

→ ingest leads → normalize data → remove duplicates → enrich accounts → research companies → collect evidence → score ICP fit → detect buying signals → identify the right buyer → generate personalization → verify every claim → get human approval → update the CRM → send safely → classify replies → stop when necessary → log every decision → recover from failures → monitor performance
Here's the full build. (1/3)
—
STEP 1 — DEFINE THE SYSTEM
The objective: turn a raw lead into a verified, human-approved sales action.
The system should be able to answer: Who is this company? Are they a fit? Why might they care now? Who owns the problem? What evidence supports that? What should we say? Is it factually safe? Should a human approve it? What happened afterward?
Build it as a state machine. Every lead has a state — and the workflow decides the state, never the AI.
Success path: NEW → ENRICHING → RESEARCHING → SCORED → PERSONALIZING → VERIFYING → PENDING_APPROVAL → APPROVED → SENT → REPLIED
Failure states: DUPLICATE, INVALID, RESEARCH_FAILED, VERIFICATION_FAILED, HUMAN_REVIEW, SUPPRESSED, SEND_FAILED
—
STEP 2 — THE ARCHITECTURE
[see image 1]
Lead Source → Normalization → Deduplication → Enrichment → Research → ICP + Intent + Buyer → Context Packet → Personalization → Fact Verifier → Human Approval → Send Gate → Email + CRM → Reply Classifier → Sales / Nurture / Suppress / Human
Build this as 8 separate n8n workflows, not one giant 100-node canvas:
01_lead_intake 02_research_and_scoring 03_personalization_and_verification 04_human_approval 05_send_gate 06_reply_handler 07_error_handler 08_monitoring
—
STEP 3 — THE STACK
n8n → orchestration PostgreSQL → state + audit history LLM → reasoning and structured generation Search/enrichment provider → external company/contact data CRM → system of record Email provider → outbound/inbound Slack → human approval
Credential rule: never put secrets inside code nodes, prompts, database records, Slack messages, or lead JSON. Use n8n's credential store / environment config only. The AI sees business data. It never sees credentials.

—

STEP 4 — THE CORE PRINCIPLE

The AI recommends. Rules validate. Humans authorize sensitive actions.

Never: AI → SEND

Always: AI → VALIDATE → VERIFY → HUMAN → SEND
The final send node needs a hard gate. Conceptually:

if (json.approval_status !== "APPROVED") { throw new Error("SEND_BLOCKED: approval required"); }

A prompt failure can never accidentally become an email.
—

STEP 5 — THE DATABASE
[see image 2]

CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS pgcrypto;

CREATE TABLE leads ( id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(), company_name TEXT NOT NULL, domain TEXT, contact_name TEXT, contact_title TEXT, email TEXT, source TEXT, status TEXT DEFAULT 'NEW', icp_score NUMERIC, intent_score NUMERIC, confidence NUMERIC, created_at TIMESTAMP DEFAULT NOW(), updated_at TIMESTAMP DEFAULT NOW() );

CREATE INDEX idx_leads_email ON leads (LOWER(email)); CREATE INDEX idx_leads_domain ON leads (LOWER(domain)); CREATE INDEX idx_leads_status ON leads (status); CREATE INDEX idx_leads_icp_score ON leads (icp_score);

Without indexes, duplicate checks and queue queries get expensive as the table grows.

Five more tables round out the schema:

research — raw structured research + evidence + sources (never store just the summary, you need the evidence later)
messages — subject/body, personalization_reason, verification_status, approval_status, human_edited_body
lead_events — the audit log: lead_id, event_type, agent, input, output, confidence, timestamp
suppressions — email/domain/reason, checked before every send
lead_state_history — previous_state, new_state, reason, timestamp for every transition
Each gets its own indexes on lead_id and the fields you'll filter on (approval_status, verification_status, email, domain).
—
STEP 6 — DEFINE THE ICP BEFORE TOUCHING AI

Don't tell the model "find good leads." Give it measurable criteria as one canonical config object, reused across every agent:

{ "industries": ["B2B SaaS", "FinTech", "Professional Services"], "employee_min": 50, "employee_max": 500, "regions": ["United States", "Canada", "United Kingdom"], "target_roles": ["CEO", "Founder", "VP Sales", "Head of Growth"], "minimum_score": 70 }

Pass this same object into the ICP scorer, the buyer mapper, the research agent, and the personalization agent. Change the ICP once — not four prompts.
—
STEP 7 — THE SCORING MODEL
Industry fit — 20 Company size — 20 Role fit — 20 Problem fit — 20 Geography — 10 Business signal — 10 TOTAL — 100
Each category must return a structured object, never a bare number:
{ "score": 0, "max": 20, "reason": "", "evidence": [] }
Never let the model just return "87." You need to know why it returned 87 — and the total should be calculated deterministically in code, not by the LLM.

Routing (numeric, never natural language like "good lead"):

85–100 → PRIORITY 70–84 → DEEPER RESEARCH 50–69 → NURTURE 0–49 → STOP

That's the foundation: architecture, stack, database, and scoring model.

Part 2 covers lead intake, enrichment, research, the verification loop, and how the writer and the fact-checker are forced to see the exact same evidence. →

VIDEO PROMPT

Use the uploaded image as the exact visual reference for the scene. Preserve the main woman's appearance, black leather jacket, gray shirt, ripped jeans, boots, the four masked skull gangsters, black muscle car, graffiti alley, red-and-blue neon lighting, smoke and cinematic atmosphere.

Create a 10-second maximum vertical/social-media-ready cinematic gangster parody.

The video must feel like a viral movie meme, not an advertisement.

0–2 SEC — HOOK

Start with an extremely dramatic cinematic push-in toward the woman sitting on the hood of the black muscle car.

Four skull-masked gangsters stand around her like an elite criminal crew.

Heavy bass.

She slowly says:

“We need one perfect image.”

Everyone looks deadly serious.

2–4 SEC — THE “HEIST”

Rapid cinematic montage:

The four gangsters suddenly sprint into action.

One kicks open a giant metal vault.

Another dramatically pulls out a laptop.

Another throws a huge stack of papers onto a table.

The woman walks into the vault like a crime boss.

The entire sequence looks like they are stealing millions of dollars.

4–6 SEC — REVEAL

The vault doors open.

Inside is something completely ridiculous:

ONE COMPUTER SCREEN

On the screen:

“GENERATING…”

Below it:

CREDITS: 03

Everyone freezes.

Extreme close-up of the woman's face.

She looks at the screen.

Then looks at the gangsters.

Dead silence.

6–8 SEC — ABSURDITY

The screen suddenly flashes:

“GENERATION FAILED.”

The four skull gangsters slowly turn toward each other.

One of them dramatically drops his laptop.

The woman sighs.

She says:

“We burned HOW many credits?”

8–10 SEC — PUNCHLINE

Suddenly the entire vault EXPLODES into hundreds of rapidly changing visual worlds:

fashion film → luxury mansion → gangster movie → futuristic city → fantasy world → surreal landscape → music video → absurd meme.

Hundreds of possibilities flash around the characters.

The woman casually walks away while the gangsters stare in disbelief.

Hard cut to black.

Small text:

“WHY BURN CREDITS?”

Immediately after:

GIMI

CINEMATOGRAPHY

Premium gangster movie cinematography mixed with absurd internet humor.

Dark urban alley.

Red and electric-blue neon.

Wet asphalt reflections.

Volumetric smoke.

Strong rim lighting.

Anamorphic lens.

Shallow depth of field.

Handheld action camera.

Fast whip-pans.

Crash zooms.

Extreme close-ups.

Realistic facial expressions.

Photorealistic 4K detail.

High-end cinematic color grading.

The contrast between serious gangster filmmaking and the ridiculous AI situation is the main joke.

EDITING

Extremely fast pacing.

No unnecessary establishing shots.

Every shot must either:

increase tension → create confusion → deliver the joke.

The first second must immediately look like an expensive crime movie.

The reveal at 4–6 seconds should completely change the meaning of the scene.

The final 2 seconds should feel like an unexpected meme and make viewers want to replay the video.

SOUND DESIGN

Start with an intense gangster soundtrack.

Deep bass.

Engine rumble.

Heavy footsteps.

Metal vault impacts.

Fast cinematic risers.

At “CREDITS: 03”, suddenly remove the music.

Complete silence.

Add one tiny computer notification sound.

At “GENERATION FAILED”, add a ridiculous dramatic impact.

Then unleash rapid glitch sounds, whooshes and cinematic impacts as hundreds of visual worlds appear.

IMPORTANT

Maximum duration: 10 seconds
Do not explain GIMI
Do not make it feel like a normal advertisement
No narrator
Minimal dialogue
Keep the woman completely cool and serious
Keep the gangsters extremely serious
Make the situation increasingly ridiculous
GIMI logo only at the very end
The phrase “WHY BURN CREDITS?” should be the only explicit marketing message
Maintain exact character consistency
Preserve the original red/blue neon gangster aesthetic
Make it feel like a scene from a $100M crime movie that suddenly turns into an absurd AI meme
The final frame should be clean and instantly recognizable @GimiApp

Today's cancer vaccine results from @moderna_tx and @Merck are exciting, confirming the earlier Phase 2 results and also the news we got a few months ago at @ASCO. 

They're also a great excuse to discuss the lifecycle of AI in the drug development process. 

All emerging technologies have a maturation lifecycle. AI  in the natural sciences is a perfect example.

On the "boring end", you have old-school ML classifiers, decision trees, SVMs, and computer vision techniques that are silently baked into every sequencing machine and molecular diagnostic workflow on the planet. Would you consider this "AI in drug development". 

No, you wouldn't. (1) Because precision diagnostics aren't drug development and (2) because these techniques don't get clustered alongside the frontier/hypey areas like 'virtual cell'. 

That's the other end of the spectrum, the "hypey end". 

These are the AI implementations that attract disproportionate venture investment, make all the headlines, and that have attached a bunch of very smart sounding reasons why they'll never work. 

They become associated with the whole. Folks will often point to them as class representatives for 'AI in drug development' as a simple way to reject the entire class's effects on the industry. 

I have an allergic reaction to this because, to me, data-driven/ML methods are inseparable from and massively contribute to the life sciences.

It's just that we don't celebrate the critical trailing edge because it's lost its sci-fi sheen, but it nonetheless serves as the foundation that all new advances become reality. 

So let's take the @moderna_tx and @Merck results. Would you consider this a success story for 'AI in drug development'? No, you probably wouldn't and I wouldn't blame you. 

It's true that cancer vaccines had/have many translational obstacles spanning delivery, supply chain, format, antigen selection, and more. It's foolish to try to decompose and assign credit to these pillars quantitatively. 

But let me zoom in to give some credit where it's due, because make no mistake, ML played a massive role.

Beyond the fact that advanced Illumina machines have onboard NVIDIA accelerators and run various deep-learning algorithms in their analysis pipelines, which provide the essential information for personalized cancer vaccines, I can offer up a few things you may not know. 

@PersonalisInc, the diagnostic partner for @Merck and @moderna_tx throughout these vaccine trials, spent years training ML algorithms on proprietary immunopeptidomics datasets (paired sequencing and mass-spec) to help with neoantigen presentation/immunogenicity prediction. 

This isn't commodity sequencing. These and other Personalis technologies enhanced by data-driven methods (e.g., enhanced HLA typing) were indispensable to this process by supplying the vaccine developers with high-fidelity mutanomes. 

We don't know everything about the handoff to Moderna (e.g. which models Personalis used versus Moderna used), but we do knew they used another algorithm in the pipeline to select the exact neoantigens to include in the vaccine formulation. 

So, I think it's safe to say that without the steady improvement in data-driven/ML/algorithmic techniques, we would not be standing here today with these results. 

Of course, we can wax poetic that 'these aren't neural networks', and you'd be making my point for me. These weren't leading edge AI implementations, which is why the fuller class of technology doesn't earn its roses here. 

But that's how this is going to happen. Non-leading AI techniques will continue creating value in drug development. Today's frontier techniques will improve, lose their association with 'hype', and folks will still move goalposts around what is AI in drug development. 

But that's the nice thing about goalpost moving. You can start to build a nice trend-line about where things are going. 

-------

*I use the term AI loosely to refer to all data-driven techniques. Don't @ me.

<The Truth4> summary essay: 
“Unknowingly, we’ve passed through four seasons.
Before putting pen to paper, I rewatched the closing essays from the previous three seasons. Every character seemed to come back to life once more—full of warmth, full of attitude.
And this season, in the truth game world, I met six completely different versions of myself again.
An Xiaoning, wearing a glass bead bracelet. All the reasoning correct, yet every result wrong. This is the fate of the Truth world.
Ning Bubble, with the specially mixed lemonade. The cup spilled, the murderer escaped. This is the small stroke of luck in the truth world.
Ningbo Weibu, the world’s number-one legs. Lost his memory, yet never forgot chivalry. This is the righteousness of the truth world.
Ningbo, who appears as a security guard but is actually a hereditary tomb guardian, protected the “treasure.” This is the belief of the truth world.
Wolf King Ning Chousha, eating meat and drinking soup as the alpha wolf. Surviving in the workplace purely through grit—this is the persistence of the truth world.
Lonely gamer Ning Ninghou, who used AI to create parents to keep him company. This is the warmth of the truth world.
This season’s characters are more complex and distinct, with more of the plot focused on their inner psychology. The Truth world is virtual, yet it is also real—and you and I are both living in it.
This season, old friends and new friends created a different kind of chemistry.
Jin—the only one this season to escape with zero votes. Super impressive. Your handwritten letter was so thoughtful.
He—not only outstanding in both physical and mental strength, but also played the murderer brilliantly, and even sent everyone juicy peaches. So sweet and warm.
Ke—the new iron tank. Stepped up to the responsibility, super reliable. Keep leading us forward from now on.
Ding—won on the very first try. Super awesome. No need to fear when the lights go out. Big brother will always be here.
Thank you all. This season was truly fulfilling.
I used to envy others who had a show that returned every year, where everyone could gather every year.
When Season 1 of The Truth began, this was something I didn’t dare to imagine.
Unexpectedly, in the blink of an eye, four seasons have passed. For me, The Truth has slowly transformed from a show into family and friends. Every recording feels like coming home—full of anticipation, completely relaxing.
And me? From turning off the lights at 1.3 meters tall to being able to stand and walk in the dark. From easily being deceived and swept along by the pace to breaking free of fixed thinking and dissecting the logic. I feel I’ve changed… yet I also haven’t changed at all.
Special thanks to Tencent Video and Zhenzhen Rishang’s screenwriters, directors, and every single staff member. It is your purity, focus, dedication, and sincerity that created such a genuine and empathetic The Truth game world.
Special thanks to everyone who has accompanied us through four seasons. Once you enter The Truth, it’s as deep as the sea. From then on, Push friends are family.
Next season.

@OpenAI @sama The false-positive image generation issue is becoming seriously disruptive.

This is NOT just ChatGPT misreading an ambiguous request like “maybe edit this image.”

I’ve had image-generation behavior trigger when:

I attached an image from X just to comment on it
I was discussing image generation as a product feature
I was asking about coding
I was literally discussing this image-generation false-positive bug

In one recent case, I was explaining why I suspect image-related requests may sometimes enter a different routing/execution path. There was ZERO request to generate an image — yet that message itself triggered the image-generation UI.

At this point, I seriously question whether the system is reliably distinguishing:

“mentions image generation”
from
“requests image generation.”
There are also consistent observable differences when this happens:
A gray image-generation UI appears

Text responses take ~20–40 seconds longer

Normal responses may show “Used 5.6 Sol,” while false-positive responses sometimes show no execution model
The writing style sometimes shifts toward patterns I strongly associate with GPT-5.4
I am NOT claiming that GPT-5.4 is definitely being used.
I am saying that multiple independent UI/behavioral changes occur at the same time, which is enough reason to ask OpenAI to inspect the internal tool-selection / routing / execution logs.

This is especially frustrating because my Custom Instructions and Memory explicitly say:

Do not generate or edit images unless I clearly ask for it.

Yet I still have to keep adding:

“⚠️ This is not an image-generation request. Respond in text only.”

And even that needs to be repeated because the behavior can return after a few turns.

This creates a real workflow cost:

**20–40 sec extra latency

interrupted concentration

defensive prompting every few turns

uncertainty about which execution path/model handled a difficult task**
For coding, research, analysis, or long-form work, that is not a trivial UI annoyance.
I reported this before and ended up being asked for HAR files, timestamps, network diagnostics, etc. For an intermittent routing/tool-selection issue, asking users to run DevTools indefinitely and act as unpaid debuggers is not a reasonable support workflow.

Please investigate this from server-side telemetry.

Image generation should require clear positive generation/editing intent, not merely the presence of an image or image-related vocabulary.

This has been happening for months.

Please fix the false-positive threshold — and please make tool/model routing more transparent.

If anyone else is seeing “I never asked for an image, but the image-generation box appeared anyway,” I’d really like to know.

Technology can be potentially* positively transformative. But don't let them conflate all machine learning with the generative AI products forced upon, devolving, and destroying the world. Public opinion often can't separate tech from products they know it as. This doesn't require an endless landscape of data centers. Even some gen AI has legitimate use, but none of it (even at its maximal potential) is worth its monumental costs.

* The asterisk on "potentially" is because society today is fundamentally built on exploitation, so tech can't be allowed to actually ease labor burdens in some utopic fashion, only benefit employers (usually by saving them money) and thrust those newly unemployed by the tech back into poverty and even more exploitable with their skillsets devalued.

Also, tech increasingly isn't allowed to be disruptive of traditional capital centers (e.g. industries). Historically, inventions have disrupted industries because discoveries were somewhat accessible to the common man. But, tech has become so advanced that further invention requires concerted effort with specialized equipment, environments, manpower, and knowledge bases exclusive to those that hold the capital!

And obviously, corporations don't want disruption. So infinite opportunities to better the world with our most incredible capabilities as a species pass by day after day to focus on reinforcing what already is. And right now, what is is not great. Another fundamental problem with capitalism. Don't mess with the capital, even when it would be in the best interest of everyone.
